items.title: Trump says Iran's leader is dead
items.description: Donald Trump has called on Iranians to "rise up" and says joint action is aimed at regime change.

items.title: Ali Khamenei mastered the art of pitting his enemies against each other
items.description: A conservative Islamic scholar with a head for politics, Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei succeeded his mentor in the wake of the Iran-Iraq War — and consolidated his grip on power over the following decades.

items.title: This strike is different and could lead to a longer, deadlier war
items.description: It was clear within hours that this conflict is different and threatens to engulf the region in a longer, deadlier war.

items.title: What we know about Iran strikes and retaliation
items.description: After weeks of anticipation, Israel fired the first shot on Iran, drawing in the US and sparking retaliatory strikes that have hit several countries.

items.title: Former prison officers speak out against culture of silence
items.description: Current and former NSW prison officers describe what they say is a toxic workplace culture and a system that shields officers accused of serious misconduct, rather than holding them accountable. They argue it has driven younger officers out of the service.

items.title: 'Shocking' reason behind 40pc of NSW's more than 200 kidnappings a year
items.description: Data shows that in the year to September 2025, NSW Police received 230 abduction and kidnapping reports — up from 224 in the previous year.

items.title: Seventh narco sub found near Australia waters signalling 'insane amount of drugs'
items.description: At least seven narco subs have been discovered in Pacific waters near Australia in the past 18 months, with experts warning that Australia's cocaine demand means more are on the way.

items.title: The 'lonely experience' of campus life as universities go digital
items.description: Two students who went to the same university 30 years apart share their radically different experiences as lectures go online and face-to-face contact takes a back seat in the post-pandemic world.

items.title: Too tall, too old, too Aussie: I'm a tough sell for arranged marriage
items.description: From Tinder-style apps to astrological birth charts — how today's arranged marriages blend tech and tradition in unexpected ways.

items.title: The Bondi terror attack changed how to buy a gun. Here's what it takes
items.description: Law reforms were swiftly passed following the massacre in December. So how difficult has it become  to legally own a firearm in the state?

items.title: Are Australians losing their sense of direction due to phone apps?
items.description: Google Maps has made city driving a dream, but it's putting lives at risk in the bush. Meet the mapmakers taking on Australia's roughest roads to try to change that.

items.title: A heaven-sent, incredibly rare event is unfolding in the outback
items.description: In the centre of Australia, there are whispers that Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre is experiencing conditions strangely similar to those that set a record depth of 6 metres in 1974.

items.title: 'We all need soft spaces': Punch the monkey's reminder
items.description: There's surely a reason we all went briefly nuts about a lonely little snow monkey called Punch living in a Japanese zoo.

items.title: In PNG's tribal warfare industry, women and drugs are traded for weapons
items.description: The proliferation of illegal high-powered guns is fuelling tribal warfare across Papua New Guinea and warlords claim children as young as eight are being trained to carry the weapons.

items.title: Get ready trivia nuts. It's time to play, HARD!
items.description: Have you been waiting all week to give this quiz another crack? You should probably find a hobby.

items.title: Some Scream fans are boycotting the new edition. Here’s why
items.description: Weinstein, copycat panic, leaked scripts, closed studios and departing stars — Scream's 30-year journey has been anything but smooth and the seventh edition in the cornerstone slasher series is no different.

items.title: From Tennessee to today: Why we still love Arrested Development
items.description: The pioneering hip hop group returns to Australia this week, with big ideas about the future of hip hop.

items.title: Your complete guide to the Matildas Women's Asian Cup squad
items.description: You know the big names — Sam Kerr, Mary Fowler, Steph Catley — but what about the emerging Matildas stars who are looking to make an impact at the Women's Asian Cup in Australia? Here's your guide to every squad member.

items.title: 'Recharge and get back to it': How respite can help carers keep going
items.description: Each Wednesday, Meika Robertson's husband Rob spends the day in respite care going on outings and chatting with others. While Rob enjoys a day away from home, Meika catches her breath.

items.title: Outback town adopts cross-country walker stranded for weeks by storms
items.description: Mark Gresser was walking from Australia's most westerly point to its most easterly point when he rolled into the NSW town of Tibooburra with the plan to stay a couple of days.

items.title: Extreme rhetoric in right-wing political circles deserves more attention
items.description: The rhetoric in Australia's right-wing political circles is getting more extreme and the media should be paying more attention.

items.title: Chef tackles food waste by cooking 'funny' meat cuts
items.description: Some high-end restaurants are turning to an uncommon practice to save money and hundreds of kilograms of beef.

items.title: 'Unbelievable' urban bowling green temperature stuns emergency services
items.description: Drones are measuring the temperatures of common surfaces in regional cities and the results have stunned emergency services, with Mount Gambier's lawn bowls turf recording a temperature of 86 degrees Celsius.

items.title: 'Transforming the system': Sweeping NSW foster care reforms announced
items.description: While some child protection services will continue to be outsourced, the NSW government will play a larger role in the sector, including through the recruitment of foster carers.

items.title: Turtle 'panel beater' saving lives with 3D printer and dental glue
items.description: When turtles are struck on country roads, their shattered shells can mean certain death, but one rescuer in Victoria's east is patching them up and sending them home.
